newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: FISCHER ON TRADE MISSION TO SOUTH ASIA
Deputy Prime Minister Tim Fischer leaves today on the most senior trade mission to south Asia since 1984.
Mr Fischer will take business leaders from 20 companies to Pakistan, Bangladesh, Nepal and Bhutan.
In Mr Fischer's absence, the Deputy Liberal leader, Peter Costello, is acting Prime Minister.
But it's only for a day, as John Howard returns from China tonight.
QLD GOVT WARNED ABOUT PRISON RIOT: OPPOSITION
The Queensland Opposition says the state Corrective Services Minister, Russell Cooper, had been warned about the riot at Woodford prison but did not act.

Opposition Corrective Service spokesman, Tom Barton, says there have been persistent rumours about a planned riot and he had put a question on notice to Mr Cooper in Parliament within the last fortnight.
Armed police and the dog squad were called to the prison north west of Brisbane as about 150 inmates lit fires and damaged property in a protest against a smoking ban and food quality.
Police and prison officers fired warning shots during the four-hour riot.
OVERNIGHT FERRY SERVICE PROPOSAL FOR SYDNEY TO MELBOURNE
A shipping company is proposing to set up a high-speed overnight ferry service between Sydney and Melbourne within two months.
The Sydney-based company, Richell's Shipping Lines, claims to have already purchased two Norwegian-built ferries, each capable of carrying up to 150 passengers at speeds of up to 50 knots.
The Australian Maritime Safety Authority says it's spoken with the company but is yet to see an application for the ferry service or arrange for sea trials of the vessels.
POLICE HOPE TO LINK SKULL TO HEADLESS BODY
Detectives are hoping post-mortem tests will establish whether a human skull found in Sydney yesterday belongs to a decapitated body discovered over a month ago.
The skull, in a weighted bag, was found in Saltpan Creek, Riverwood, by an angler.
In February, a headless body was found floating in Paddy's River off the Hume Highway, near Marulen, in the southern highlands.
A police spokeswoman says the post-mortem tests will be conducted tomorrow. - - - -
VICTIMS RIGHTS ACT CONCERNS
In New South Wales, a civil rights network is concerned the new Victims Rights Act could lead to inconsistent sentencing, but still supports the Act.
From today, the Act will allow victims to submit a statement to the courts.
The Victims and Civil Rights Project's Tim Anderson says members are concerned that without controls, victims' impact statements could make a mockery of the justice system.
Mr Anderson says it needs has to be made very clear offenders are not going to be sentenced according to how much noise is made against them.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
